# Task
Implement AudioManager with music crossfade

Implement autoloads/audio_manager.gd with two AudioStreamPlayer nodes for music (music_a, music_b). Crossfade: play_music(track, fade_duration=1.0): if music_a playing, start music_b with new track at volume 0, tween music_a to 0 and music_b to target volume over fade_duration, swap roles. Music tracks loaded from assets/audio/music/ by name. Music plays at reduced volume during battles (or switches to battle music). SFX pool: 8 AudioStreamPlayer nodes for concurrent effects, play_sfx(sfx): find idle player, load and play. Cry player: dedicated AudioStreamPlayer, play_cry(dex_number): load assets/audio/cries/{dex_number}.ogg. Cries play on encounter, send-out, Pokedex view. Audio manager provides centralized audio control.

    index.ts          — Express entry point, registers all routes

# Test Specification for Natures JSON

## Overview
Created comprehensive test suite for the natures JSON data file and its integration with Pokemon stat calculations.

## Test Files Created

### 1. `tests/unit/test_natures.gd`
Tests the structure and content of `data/pokemon/natures.json`.

**Test Coverage:**
- File existence and parsing
- Contains all 25 official Pokemon natures
- Each nature has required fields (`increased_stat`, `decreased_stat`)
- Neutral natures (5): Hardy, Docile, Bashful, Quirky, Serious
- Non-neutral natures (20): All stat combinations
- Specific nature verifications (Adamant, Modest, Jolly, Timid, Bold, Calm)
- Stat name validation (only: atk, def, spa, spd, spe)
- HP is never affected by natures
- Each stat has exactly 5 boosting and 5 lowering natures
- Complete 5×5 nature matrix (all combinations present)
- No extra/invalid natures beyond the official 25

**Total Test Methods:** 16

### 2. `tests/unit/test_pokemon_instance_natures.gd`
Tests that `PokemonInstance.get_stat()` correctly applies nature modifiers.

**Test Coverage:**
- Neutral natures produce identical stats
- Specific nature effects:
  - Adamant: +10% Atk, -10% SpA
  - Modest: +10% SpA, -10% Atk
  - Jolly: +10% Spe, -10% SpA
  - Timid: +10% Spe, -10% Atk
  - Bold: +10% Def, -10% Atk
  - Calm: +10% SpD, -10% Atk
- HP is never affected by natures
- Nature modifiers only affect specified stats
- All 25 natures can be applied without errors
- Nature scaling works at different levels (1-100)
- Nature modifiers apply after IVs and EVs
- Opposite natures have opposite effects
- Invalid nature handling (graceful fallback)

**Total Test Methods:** 17

## Expected Test Failures

When run without implementation, tests should fail with:

1. **test_natures.gd:**
   - `test_natures_file_exists_and_loads()`: FAIL - File not found at `res://data/pokemon/natures.json`
   - All other tests: FAIL - `natures_data` is empty dictionary

2. **test_pokemon_instance_natures.gd:**
   - All tests: FAIL - Cannot load resource `res://resources/pokemon_instance.gd` (file does not exist)
   - Or: Cannot load resource `res://resources/pokemon_species.gd` (file does not exist)

**These are the correct failure modes** - "implementation missing", not syntax errors in test files.

# Task
Implement LAN server discovery with UDP broadcast

Extend autoloads/network_manager.gd with discover_servers(). Host broadcasts UDP packet every 2s to 255.255.255.255:7999 containing JSON: {game, version, host_name, player_count, max_players, port}. Clients bind PacketPeerUDP to port 7999 with broadcast enabled, check for packets in _process, parse JSON, emit EventBus.server_discovered(server_info). Maintain discovered server list with 6s TTL (remove if no broadcast received). This enables automatic LAN game discovery - critical for iOS where manual IP entry is cumbersome.

# Task
Implement LAN server discovery with UDP broadcast

Extend autoloads/network_manager.gd with discover_servers(). Host broadcasts UDP packet every 2s to 255.255.255.255:7999 containing JSON: {game, version, host_name, player_count, max_players, port}. Clients bind PacketPeerUDP to port 7999 with broadcast enabled, check for packets in _process, parse JSON, emit EventBus.server_discovered(server_info). Maintain discovered server list with 6s TTL (remove if no broadcast received). This enables automatic LAN game discovery - critical for iOS where manual IP entry is cumbersome.

# Task
Implement LAN server discovery with UDP broadcast

Extend autoloads/network_manager.gd with discover_servers(). Host broadcasts UDP packet every 2s to 255.255.255.255:7999 containing JSON: {game, version, host_name, player_count, max_players, port}. Clients bind PacketPeerUDP to port 7999 with broadcast enabled, check for packets in _process, parse JSON, emit EventBus.server_discovered(server_info). Maintain discovered server list with 6s TTL (remove if no broadcast received). This enables automatic LAN game discovery - critical for iOS where manual IP entry is cumbersome.

task.description: Install GUT addon to addons/gut/ directory and configure for headless CLI execution. Create gut_config.json to enable command-line test running. GUT will be used throughout development for unit and integration testing, so this must work before any test-driven development begins. CRITICAL: Godot binary is /Applications/Godot_mono.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot on macOS (no godot on PATH). task.title: Install and configure GdUnit4 test framework
task.description: Install GdUnit4 addon to addons/gdunit4/ directory. Verify it runs headlessly alongside GUT. Both test frameworks will be used: GUT for integration tests and GdUnit4 for unit tests. Create a simple GdUnit4 test to validate setup. Ensure both frameworks coexist without conflicts. CRITICAL: Godot binary is /Applications/Godot_mono.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot on macOS (no godot on PATH). Any headless Godot invocation MUST pass --path "$PWD" and -s <script.gd>. Omitting -s pops a blocking macOS GUI modal and freezes the session.

task.title: Create autoload singleton scaffolds
task.description: Create the 5 core autoload singletons as empty GDScript files and register them in project.godot under [autoload]: GameManager (top-level FSM), NetworkManager (ENet networking), EventBus (signal hub), AudioManager (music/SFX), DataRegistry (game data loader). Each should be a minimal class extending Node with a _ready() function that prints its name. These singletons form the architectural backbone - all game systems will interact through these autoloads.

task.title: Create main scene and title screen scaffold
task.description: Create main.tscn as the root scene (a Node with main.gd script) that transitions to title_screen.tscn. Create a basic title_screen.tscn with a centered Label showing 'Pokemon LAN Battle Royale' and placeholder buttons for Host/Join. The main scene should be set as the project's main scene in project.godot. This establishes the scene management pattern and entry point for the application.

task.title: Configure iOS export preset
task.description: Create export_presets.cfg with iOS export configuration: bundle ID (com.yourname.pokemonbr), provisioning profile placeholder, minimum iOS 15.0, landscape orientation, required entitlements including com.apple.developer.networking.multicast for UDP broadcast. Configure app icons and launch screen. Add NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription to Info.plist template. This enables building for iOS - critical for the target platform.

task.title: Set up CI pipeline for headless testing
task.description: Create .github/workflows/test.yml using barichello/godot-ci Docker image to run GUT and GdUnit4 tests headlessly on every push. Configure the workflow to use Godot 4.4.x, run all tests in tests/ directory, and report results. This ensures all code changes are automatically validated, catching regressions early.

task.title: Define PokemonSpecies custom resource
task.description: Create resources/pokemon_species.gd as a custom Resource class with class_name PokemonSpecies. Properties: dex_number (int), name (String), types (Array[String]), base_stats (Dictionary with hp/atk/def/spa/spd/spe), abilities (Array[String]), learnset (Dictionary level->move_id), catch_rate (int), base_exp (int), growth_rate (String), egg_groups (Array[String]), sprite_front (String), sprite_back (String), cry (String). This resource will be instantiated for all 151 Gen 1 Pokemon and queried constantly during gameplay.

task.title: Define PokemonInstance custom resource
task.description: Create resources/pokemon_instance.gd as a custom Resource class with class_name PokemonInstance. This represents a specific Pokemon with individuality: species (PokemonSpecies), nickname (String), level (int), nature (String), ability (String), held_item (String), moves (Array[String] max 4), current_pp (Array[int]), ivs (Dictionary), evs (Dictionary), current_hp (int), status (String), stat_stages (Dictionary), is_fainted (bool). Include methods: get_stat(stat_name)->int (calculate from base/IV/EV/nature/level), calculate_max_hp()->int, heal_full(), apply_damage(amount), serialize()->Dictionary, deserialize(data). This is the core data structure for all Pokemon in the game - battles, catches, parties all use PokemonInstance.

task.title: Define MoveData, ItemData, and AbilityData resources
task.description: Create three custom Resource classes: resources/move_data.gd (MoveData with id, name, type, category, power, accuracy, pp, priority, target, effect, effect_chance, stat_changes, status_inflict, flags), resources/item_data.gd (ItemData with id, name, category, effect, value, description, sprite, usable_in_battle, usable_in_field), resources/ability_data.gd (AbilityData with id, name, description, trigger, effect). These resources define all game content - moves pokemon can use, items players can collect, and abilities that trigger during battle.

task.title: Create type chart JSON data
task.description: Create data/type_chart.json with an 18x18 type effectiveness matrix. Keys are attacking types (normal, fire, water, electric, grass, ice, fighting, poison, ground, flying, psychic, bug, rock, ghost, dragon, dark, steel, fairy), values are dictionaries mapping defending type to multiplier (0, 0.5, 1, 2). Reference the official Pokemon type chart - accuracy is critical as this affects every battle damage calculation. Include test cases for known interactions: Fire>Grass=2x, Water>Fire=2x, Normal>Ghost=0x.

task.title: Create Pokemon registry JSON for Gen 1
task.description: Create data/pokemon/pokemon_registry.json with all 151 Gen 1 Pokemon. Each entry needs: dex_number, name, types, base_stats (hp/atk/def/spa/spd/spe), abilities (Gen 3+ ability list), learnset (level-up moves for Gen 3), catch_rate, base_exp, growth_rate, egg_groups, sprite paths. Source data from PokeAPI or Veekun pokedex database. This is a large data entry task but foundational - all Pokemon content depends on this registry being complete and accurate.

task.title: Create move registry JSON
task.description: Create data/moves/move_registry.json with ~200 moves covering all types and categories. Each entry: id, name, type, category (Physical/Special/Status), power, accuracy, pp, priority, target, effect description, effect_chance, stat_changes dict, status_inflict, flags array. Include all moves referenced in Gen 1 Pokemon learnsets. Reference Pokemon Showdown or Bulbapedia for accurate move data. Moves are used constantly in battle - accuracy matters. IMPORTANT: incremental write strategy required. The dataset is too large to materialize in one pass — DO NOT think the entire registry through before writing. Instead: (1) Write data/moves/move_registry.json with the JSON skeleton + first 20 moves immediately. (2) Then Edit-append remaining moves in batches of 20-30 at a time, committing the file with each batch. Never accumulate 200+ items in extended thinking before writing — that exhausts the output token budget.

task.title: Create item and ability registries
task.description: Create data/items/item_registry.json (~50 items: Pokeballs, Potions, Status heals, Revives, Battle items, Held items) and data/abilities/ability_registry.json (~50 common abilities: Overgrow, Blaze, Torrent, Intimidate, Levitate, Static, Poison Point, Thick Fat, Sturdy, etc.). Each item needs: id, name, category, effect, value, description, sprite path, usage flags. Each ability needs: id, name, description, trigger type, effect description. These registries enable the item system and ability-triggered battle mechanics. IMPORTANT: incremental write strategy required. Two separate registry files (~50 each). For each file: (1) Write the JSON skeleton + first 15-20 entries immediately. (2) Then Edit-append remaining entries in batches of 15-20, committing the file with each batch. Never accumulate all entries in extended thinking before writing — that exhausts the output token budget. Write items first, then abilities.

task.title: Create natures JSON
task.description: Create data/pokemon/natures.json with all 25 Pokemon natures and their stat modifiers (increased stat, decreased stat). Examples: Adamant (+Atk -SpA), Modest (+SpA -Atk), Jolly (+Spe -SpA), Timid (+Spe -Atk), Hardy (neutral). Natures affect stat calculations in PokemonInstance.get_stat() and add strategic depth to Pokemon individuality.

task.title: Implement DataRegistry autoload
task.description: Implement autoloads/data_registry.gd to load all JSON data files at _ready(): type_chart.json, pokemon_registry.json, move_registry.json, item_registry.json, ability_registry.json, natures.json. Parse each into typed dictionaries (pokemon_db: Dictionary[String, PokemonSpecies], etc.). Implement accessor methods: get_pokemon(id), get_move(id), get_item(id), get_ability(id), get_type_effectiveness(atk_type, def_types[])->float (multiplies across dual types), get_encounter_table(zone_id). Include error handling: print warnings for missing data, assert on critical failures. This is the single source of truth - every system queries DataRegistry for game data.

task.title: Implement Config autoload
task.description: Implement autoloads/config.gd to load data/config/game_balance.json and data/config/round_config.json. Expose constants: ROAMING_TIMER_SECONDS, BASE_CATCH_RATE_MODIFIER, WILD_ENCOUNTER_CHANCE, MAX_PARTY_SIZE (6), MIN_PLAYERS, MAX_PLAYERS, action timers, loot phase duration, per-round settings. These values will be tuned during balance phase but need default values now. Config provides gameplay tuning without code changes.

task.title: Write unit tests for data loading and validation
task.description: Create tests/unit/test_data_loading.gd to verify: all JSON files parse without error, all Pokemon have valid types (exist in type chart), all moves referenced in learnsets exist in move registry, all abilities referenced exist in ability registry, no duplicate IDs. Create tests/unit/test_type_chart.gd to verify known effectiveness values (Fire>Grass=2x, Water>Fire=2x, Normal>Ghost=0x) and dual-type multiplication (Fire>Grass/Poison=4x). Create tests/unit/test_pokemon_instance.gd to verify stat calculation matches official formula, nature modifiers apply correctly, serialize/deserialize round-trips. These tests prevent data corruption and ensure formula accuracy.

task.title: Implement NetworkManager host and join functions
task.description: Implement autoloads/network_manager.gd with host_game(player_name, port=7000) and join_game(address, port=7000). Host: create ENetMultiplayerPeer with create_server(port, 8), assign to multiplayer.multiplayer_peer, add self (peer ID 1) to players dict, connect peer_connected/peer_disconnected signals. Join: create ENetMultiplayerPeer with create_client(address, port), connect connected_to_server, connection_failed, server_disconnected signals. Store players: Dictionary[int, PlayerData] keyed by peer ID. This establishes the networking foundation - all multiplayer features depend on reliable host/join.

task.title: Implement LAN server discovery with UDP broadcast
task.description: Extend autoloads/network_manager.gd with discover_servers(). Host broadcasts UDP packet every 2s to 255.255.255.255:7999 containing JSON: {game, version, host_name, player_count, max_players, port}. Clients bind PacketPeerUDP to port 7999 with broadcast enabled, check for packets in _process, parse JSON, emit EventBus.server_discovered(server_info). Maintain discovered server list with 6s TTL (remove if no broadcast received). This enables automatic LAN game discovery - critical for iOS where manual IP entry is cumbersome.

task.title: Implement player info exchange and ready state RPCs
task.description: Add RPC methods to autoloads/network_manager.gd: @rpc('any_peer','reliable') _register_player(info) for clients to send their info to server, @rpc('authority','reliable') _sync_player_list(all_players) for server to broadcast full player list to all clients, @rpc('any_peer','reliable') _set_ready(peer_id, is_ready) to toggle ready status. Server maintains authoritative player list and broadcasts updates. Handle peer_disconnected: remove from players dict, broadcast updated list, emit EventBus.player_left. Handle server_disconnected (client side): return to title screen with error message. This manages lobby state synchronization.

task.title: Create lobby scene with player list and ready system
task.description: Create scenes/lobby/lobby.tscn with UI: header showing room code/IP, ScrollContainer with player_card.tscn instances, avatar selector carousel, name LineEdit, ready ToggleButton, start button (host only, enabled when all ready), player count label, back button. Create scenes/lobby/player_card.tscn for individual player entries (avatar icon, name label, ready indicator). Implement scenes/lobby/lobby.gd to sync with NetworkManager: display all connected players, update ready states, host can start game with @rpc('authority','call_local','reliable') _start_game() when conditions met. This is the pre-game gathering point where players prepare before entering the battle royale.

task.title: Enhance title screen with host/join/discovery UI
task.description: Enhance scenes/title/title_screen.tscn with: Host Game button (creates server, transitions to lobby), Join Game button (shows server browser panel), server browser list showing discovered LAN servers (host name, player count, tap to join), manual IP entry option, Settings button. Implement scenes/title/title_screen.gd to call NetworkManager.discover_servers(), listen for EventBus.server_discovered, populate browser list, handle host/join/browse interactions. This is the entry point for multiplayer - must be intuitive and handle iOS permission denial gracefully (fall back to manual IP).

task.title: Write networking tests for discovery and lobby sync
task.description: Create tests/network/test_server_discovery.gd (integration test requiring two instances: A hosts, B discovers A within 3s, validate packet contents), tests/network/test_lobby_sync.gd (A hosts, B joins, both see each other, B sets ready, A sees update, A starts game, both receive game_starting signal), tests/network/test_disconnect_handling.gd (A hosts, B joins, B disconnects, A updates player list; B sees server disconnected if A quits). Create ci/scripts/multi_instance_test.sh to launch multiple Godot instances for automated network testing. These tests validate the networking foundation before building gameplay on top.

task.title: Import GBA tilesets and create TileSet resources
task.description: Import GBA tileset PNGs (from Spriters Resource FRLG) into assets/sprites/tilesets/. Create Godot TileSet resources in the editor: define terrain sets for auto-tiling (grass, paths, water, buildings), set collision shapes on solid tiles, create custom data layers (walkable:bool, encounter_zone:String, transition_target:String). Tag tiles appropriately. This creates the visual foundation for all maps - players will spend most of their time navigating these tiles.

task.title: Create map base scene template
task.description: Create scenes/world/maps/map_base.tscn with: root Node2D with map_base.gd script, child TileMapLayer nodes (Ground, GroundOverlay, Objects, AbovePlayer for tree tops/roofs), Marker2D nodes for spawn points (player/item/NPC), Area2D nodes for zones (tall grass, transitions, healing stations). Export variables: map_id, map_display_name, encounter_table_id. Create scenes/world/maps/map_base.gd to expose these. This template will be inherited by all specific maps (town_01, route_01, cave_01, forest_01), providing consistent structure.

task.title: Build four starter maps
task.description: Create four maps inheriting from map_base.tscn: scenes/world/maps/town_01.tscn (starting town with Pokemon Center, open areas, few tall grass patches), route_01.tscn (connecting route with abundant tall grass, scattered items), cave_01.tscn (cave with different encounter table, narrower paths), forest_01.tscn (dense forest with heavy encounter zones). Design layouts using TileMapLayers, place spawn point Marker2Ds, define encounter Area2Ds. Create companion JSON files in data/maps/map_defs/ for each map defining item spawn locations (item IDs, respawn timers), NPC placements (team IDs from npc_teams.json), encounter zone definitions. These maps provide the play spaces for exploration and wild encounters.

task.title: Create player character with movement and animation
task.description: Create scenes/world/player/player_character.tscn: root CharacterBody2D with player_character.gd, Sprite2D/AnimatedSprite2D with 4-directional walk cycle animations (idle_down/up/left/right, walk_down/up/left/right), CollisionShape2D at feet, Area2D named InteractionZone (detects interactables in facing direction), MultiplayerSynchronizer syncing position/current_animation/facing_direction, Label for nametag. Implement player_character.gd: grid-based movement (16-32px per step, smooth tween, ~4 tiles/sec), input handling (virtual joystick or keyboard), only process input if is_multiplayer_authority(), set animation based on movement, tall grass detection (step on grass tile -> notify server to roll encounter), map transition handling, interaction logic (A button -> raycast/Area2D check -> emit EventBus.player_interacted). This is the player's avatar in the world - movement feel is critical.

task.title: Create remote player rendering
task.description: Create scenes/world/player/remote_player.tscn: simplified player_character (no input processing), MultiplayerSynchronizer receives position/animation state from authority, renders sprite and nametag, smooth interpolation for network jitter (position = position.lerp(sync_position, delta * 10)). This represents other players' avatars as seen by the local client - must smoothly display networked movement.

task.title: Create virtual joystick for touch controls
task.description: Create scenes/ui/hud/virtual_joystick.tscn: TouchScreenButton-based or custom Control node with outer ring (static or follows initial touch), inner knob (follows finger), outputs normalized Vector2 direction, supports 4-directional snapping for GBA feel, configurable dead zone, haptic feedback on direction change. Add A/B buttons (A=interact/confirm, B=cancel/run) on right side, pause/menu button in corner. Implement scenes/ui/hud/virtual_joystick.gd to handle touch input and output direction. This enables mobile-friendly controls - critical for iOS target platform.

task.title: Create game camera with smooth follow
task.description: Create scenes/world/camera/game_camera.tscn: Camera2D with position_smoothing_enabled=true (speed ~5), pixel-perfect snapping for GBA feel (position snapped to Vector2(1,1) each frame), limits set to map boundaries (configured per map or auto-calculated from TileMapLayer used rect), zoom level for appropriate GBA viewport feel (test to find right value). Implement scenes/world/camera/game_camera.gd to follow local player's position. The camera provides the player's view into the world - smooth following prevents motion sickness.

task.title: Create world scene with player spawning
task.description: Create scenes/world/world.tscn: root Node2D with world.gd, child for active map instance (loaded dynamically), MultiplayerSpawner configured to spawn player_character.tscn, CanvasLayer for HUD overlay, game_camera.tscn following local player. Implement scenes/world/world.gd: on load, server spawns player_character for each connected player at map spawn points, sets multiplayer authority (set_multiplayer_authority(peer_id)) so only owning client controls each, MultiplayerSpawner replicates to all clients, manages map transitions (server loads new map, repositions players), spawns ground items at locations from map def JSON. This orchestrates the shared world state.

task.title: Write player position sync tests
task.description: Create tests/network/test_player_position_sync.gd: integration test with two instances, player A moves, player B sees A move within 100ms, positions converge. Manual playtest checklist: walk around maps on two devices, verify collision with walls, verify camera follows, verify nametags display, verify virtual joystick feels responsive. Create tests/ui/test_virtual_joystick.gd using GodotTestDriver to simulate touch input and verify joystick outputs correct direction vectors. Performance test: verify 8 player sprites on screen maintain 60fps on target iOS device. These tests validate the world foundation before adding encounters and battles.

task.title: Create encounter table resource and data files
task.description: Create resources/encounter_table.gd: custom Resource with class_name EncounterTable, properties: entries (Array[Dictionary]) where each has pokemon_id, min_level, max_level, weight. Create data/encounter_tables/ JSON files for each zone: route_1.json, cave_1.json, forest_1.json with Pokemon appropriate to that area and weighted spawn rates. These tables define what wild Pokemon appear where - variety and balance matter for gameplay pacing.

task.title: Implement wild encounter spawner logic
task.description: Create scenes/world/npcs/wild_pokemon_spawner.gd (server-side logic): when player steps on tall grass tile (detected by player_character), server rolls encounter check (randf() < Config.WILD_ENCOUNTER_CHANCE ~0.15 per step). If triggers, select Pokemon from zone's encounter table using weighted random, generate PokemonInstance with random IVs (0-31), random nature, moves from learnset appropriate to level. Send @rpc('authority','reliable') _trigger_encounter(player_peer_id, pokemon_data) to encountering player. This creates the wild encounter mechanic - the primary way players build their teams.

task.title: Create encounter transition animation
task.description: Create scenes/encounter/encounter_transition.tscn: full-screen ColorRect or Sprite2D with shader animation, GBA-style rapid diagonal stripes or spiral wipe to black, hold briefly, reveal battle scene. Use AnimationPlayer or Tween, duration ~1.5s total (fast and punchy). Play encounter sound effect. This transition builds anticipation and provides visual feedback for the random encounter trigger.

task.title: Create simplified wild battle scene
task.description: Create scenes/encounter/wild_battle_scene.tscn (simplified for catching - full battle engine comes later): background (gradient or themed per zone), enemy Pokemon front sprite (centered upper area, slide-in), player Pokemon back sprite (centered lower area, slide-in), HP bars for both, text box at bottom, action menu (FIGHT/BAG/POKEMON/RUN). For now, FIGHT is simplified: pick move, damage calculated, turn resolves. BAG shows Pokeballs (triggers catch). POKEMON switches active. RUN attempts flee (speed-based success). Implement scenes/encounter/wild_battle_scene.gd to orchestrate this simplified battle. This provides a functional encounter system before the full battle engine is ready.

task.title: Implement catch mechanic with formula and animation
task.description: Create scenes/encounter/catch_mechanic.gd implementing official catch rate formula: catch_value = ((3*max_hp - 2*current_hp) * catch_rate * ball_modifier) / (3*max_hp) * status_modifier. Ball modifiers: Pokeball=1, Great=1.5, Ultra=2, Master=255. Status modifiers: Sleep/Freeze=2, Para/Burn/Poison=1.5. Shake check: shake_probability = 65536 / (255/catch_value)^(1/4), four shake checks, return 0-3 shakes or 4 for caught. Create scenes/encounter/pokeball_animation.tscn: ball arcs from bottom to Pokemon (parabolic tween), Pokemon shrinks into ball (scale tween + flash), ball drops and shakes 0-3 times with wobble, if caught: stars/sparkle particles + 'Gotcha!' text, if broke free: ball opens + Pokemon reappears. Sound effects for each phase. Catching Pokemon is a core mechanic - the formula must match the official games.

task.title: Implement party management system
task.description: Extend resources/player_data.gd (or create if not exists) with party: Array[PokemonInstance] max 6. When Pokemon caught: if party < 6, add to party; if full, prompt to swap or discard (for BR, force swap with UI). Create scenes/ui/menus/party_view.tscn: shows all Pokemon in party with icons, names, levels, HP bars, tap to see summary, drag to reorder (optional). Implement scenes/ui/menus/party_view.gd to display and manage party. At round start, each player receives a starter Pokemon (level 5) - server generates 3 random starters per player, player picks one (classic starter selection). Party management is critical - players need clear visibility and control of their team.

task.title: Write encounter and catch tests
task.description: Create tests/unit/test_encounter_tables.gd: load encounter table, roll 10000 encounters, verify distribution matches weights within statistical tolerance. Create tests/unit/test_catch_rate.gd: test formula with known inputs (Master Ball always catches, Pokeball on full HP legendary very low, Pokeball on 1HP sleeping Caterpie very high). Create tests/integration/test_wild_encounter_flow.gd: player steps on grass, encounter triggers, battle scene loads, player throws ball, Pokemon caught, added to party, returns to overworld. Create tests/unit/test_pokemon_instance.gd: verify random IV generation (0-31), nature application, move selection from learnset by level. These tests validate the encounter and catch mechanics work correctly.

task.title: Create battle context and data structures
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/battle_context.gd: holds all battle state with player_side (BattleSide), opponent_side (BattleSide), weather (String: none/sun/rain/sandstorm/hail), weather_turns (int), field_effects (Dictionary for entry hazards/screens), turn_number (int). Define BattleSide class: trainer_name, party (Array[PokemonInstance]), active_pokemon_index, is_npc, peer_id. Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/battle_action.gd: enum ActionType {MOVE, SWITCH, ITEM, FLEE}, properties: action_type, move_index, switch_target_index, item_id, source_side. These data structures represent all battle state - completely independent of scene tree for testability.

task.title: Implement damage calculator with official formula
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/battle_calculator.gd with calculate_damage(attacker: PokemonInstance, defender: PokemonInstance, move: MoveData, context: BattleContext) -> DamageResult. Implement official Pokemon damage formula: level_factor = (2*level/5+2), stat selection (Physical: Atk/Def, Special: SpA/SpD), apply stat stages (stages -6 to +6 map to multipliers 2/8 through 8/2), base_damage = floor((floor(level_factor * power * A/D)/50)+2), modifiers (multiplicative): STAB 1.5x if attacker type matches move, type effectiveness from DataRegistry, critical hit 1.5x (crit chance by stage: 1/24, 1/8, 1/2, 1/1), random factor randf_range(0.85,1.0), Burn 0.5x for physical if burned (unless Guts), Weather (Sun boosts Fire 1.5x weakens Water 0.5x, Rain opposite), held item modifiers (Life Orb 1.3x, Choice items 1.5x, type-boosting), ability modifiers (Blaze/Torrent/Overgrow at 1/3 HP). Return DamageResult: damage (int), effectiveness (float), is_critical (bool), type_message (String). Also implement calculate_accuracy(attacker, move, context) -> bool: base_accuracy * accuracy_stage / evasion_stage, account for abilities like Compound Eyes. This is the heart of battle calculations - must be pixel-perfect accurate to official games.

task.title: Implement status effects system
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/status_effects.gd with: apply_status(pokemon, status, context) -> bool (check type immunities: Electric immune to Paralysis, Fire to Burn, Poison/Steel to Poison, Ice to Freeze; ability immunities: Limber/Water Veil/Immunity; can't apply if already has non-volatile status), process_end_of_turn_status(pokemon) -> Array[BattleEvent] (Burn: lose 1/16 max HP, Poison: 1/8, Badly Poisoned: 1/16*N increasing, Sandstorm/Hail: 1/16 for non-immune types), check_status_prevention(pokemon, action) -> StatusCheckResult (Sleep: can't move, decrement counter 1-3 turns; Paralysis: 25% can't move; Freeze: 20% thaw chance, Fire moves thaw; Confusion: 33% hurt self with 40 power typeless physical). Status effects add strategic depth and must work exactly as in official games.

task.title: Implement stat stages system
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/stat_stages.gd: each Pokemon tracks stages for Atk/Def/SpA/SpD/Spe/Accuracy/Evasion (-6 to +6). Implement modify_stat_stage(pokemon, stat, stages) -> BattleEvent: clamp to -6/+6, return appropriate message ('Attack rose sharply!', 'Defense can't go any lower!'). Account for abilities: Clear Body prevents opponent drops, Contrary reverses, Simple doubles. Implement get_stat_stage_multiplier(stage) -> float mapping -6 to +6 to multipliers. Implement reset_stat_stages(pokemon): called on switch-out. Stat stages are a core battle mechanic affecting every turn.

task.title: Implement weather system
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/weather_system.gd with: set_weather(weather, duration, context) -> BattleEvent, process_weather_end_of_turn(context) -> Array[BattleEvent] (damage non-immune Pokemon, decrement duration), get_weather_modifier(weather, move_type) -> float (Sun boosts Fire weakens Water, Rain opposite). Check abilities on switch-in: Drought (auto-Sun), Drizzle (auto-Rain), Sand Stream (auto-Sandstorm), Snow Warning (auto-Hail). Weather affects damage calculations and end-of-turn damage - must integrate with battle flow.

task.title: Implement ability handler system
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/ability_handler.gd: abilities trigger at specific hook points (on_switch_in, on_before_move, on_after_move, on_hit_received, on_status_attempt, on_end_of_turn, on_stat_change_attempt, on_faint). Use match/dictionary dispatch pattern. Implement ~30 most common abilities: stat-altering (Intimidate, Speed Boost, Moxie), weather (Drought, Drizzle, Sand Stream, Snow Warning), type immunities (Levitate, Flash Fire, Lightning Rod, Storm Drain, Water/Volt Absorb), status (Limber, Water Veil, Immunity, Insomnia, Own Tempo), damage (Overgrow/Blaze/Torrent/Swarm, Huge Power, Pure Power, Guts, Hustle), defensive (Sturdy, Multiscale, Marvel Scale, Thick Fat), contact (Static, Poison Point, Flame Body, Rough Skin), misc (Compound Eyes, Clear Body, Contrary, Simple, Mold Breaker). Each ability effect is a method dispatched by ability ID. Abilities add strategic variety - implementation must be hook-based to integrate with battle flow.

task.title: Implement held item handler system
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/held_item_handler.gd: similar hook-based dispatch as abilities. Hook points: on_damage_calc, on_after_move, on_end_of_turn, on_hit_received, on_switch_in. Implement items: Choice Band/Specs/Scarf (1.5x Atk/SpA/Spe, locked into first move), Life Orb (1.3x damage, lose 1/10 HP after attacking), Leftovers (heal 1/16 HP end of turn), Berries (Sitrus: heal 1/4 HP at 1/2 HP, status-curing, type-resist), Focus Sash (survive OHKO at full HP with 1 HP), Eviolite (1.5x Def/SpD for not-fully-evolved), type-boosting items (Charcoal, Mystic Water, etc.), Rocky Helmet (attacker takes 1/6 HP on contact). Held items provide customization and tactical options.

task.title: Implement move effect handler for secondary effects
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/move_effects.gd (or integrate into battle_resolver) with process_move_secondary_effect(move, attacker, defender, context) -> Array[BattleEvent]. Handle effect types: stat changes (Psychic 10% SpD drop), status infliction (Thunderbolt 10% Paralyze), flinch (Rock Slide 30%), recoil (Take Down 1/4 recoil), drain (Giga Drain heal 1/2 damage), multi-hit (Double Slap 2-5 hits), fixed damage (Seismic Toss = level), OHKO (Sheer Cold accuracy=30%), priority (Quick Attack +1, Extreme Speed +2), self stat boost (Dragon Dance +1 Atk +1 Spe). Status moves: Swords Dance (+2 Atk), Toxic (badly poison), Thunder Wave (paralyze), Stealth Rock (entry hazard). Each unique effect pattern is a handler function, moves reference effect by ID. Move effects create variety in battle - comprehensive implementation needed.

task.title: Implement battle resolver for turn resolution
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/battle_resolver.gd with resolve_turn(action_player, action_opponent, context) -> Array[BattleEvent]. Turn resolution order: (1) Determine order: switches first, items second, flee attempts second, moves by priority bracket then Speed stat (account for Paralysis halving Speed, Choice Scarf, Trick Room). (2) For each action: SWITCH (switch Pokemon, trigger on_switch_in abilities, apply entry hazards), ITEM (apply effect: heal HP, cure status, boost stat), FLEE (wild only, calculate based on Speed), MOVE (check status prevention sleep/para/freeze/confusion, check accuracy, if hit: calculate damage, apply damage, check faint, process secondary effects, process abilities triggered on hit Static/Rough Skin, process held items Rocky Helmet/Focus Sash, deduct PP). (3) End of turn: weather damage, status damage burn/poison, held item effects Leftovers/Black Sludge, ability effects Speed Boost, check faints from residual. (4) If fainted, check if trainer has remaining Pokemon (yes: prompt switch, no: battle ends). Each step produces BattleEvent objects. This is the core battle logic orchestrator - correctness is critical.

task.title: Create battle event system
task.description: Define BattleEvent as simple data class: type (String), data (Dictionary). Event types: move_used, damage_dealt, stat_changed, status_applied, status_cured, weather_changed, pokemon_fainted, pokemon_switched, item_used, ability_triggered, critical_hit, effectiveness_message, battle_end, flee_success, flee_fail, pokemon_caught, text_message. The battle scene consumes events sequentially and animates each. This decouples battle logic (battle_resolver) from battle visuals (battle_scene), enabling pure data testing and flexible animation.

task.title: Implement battle state machine
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_engine/battle_state_machine.gd: states INTRO -> ACTION_SELECT -> WAITING_FOR_OPPONENT (PvP only) -> TURN_RESOLVE -> ANIMATE_EVENTS -> CHECK_FAINT -> FORCE_SWITCH -> (loop to ACTION_SELECT) -> BATTLE_END. INTRO: play intro animations (trainer slide-in, Pokemon send-out), display 'Trainer X wants to battle!' or 'A wild Y appeared!'. ACTION_SELECT: show action menu (Fight/Bag/Pokemon/Run), player selects (PvP: both select simultaneously, server resolves). TURN_RESOLVE: server calls battle_resolver.resolve_turn() to get events. ANIMATE_EVENTS: events played one by one with animations, skippable with B button (fast-forward). CHECK_FAINT: if Pokemon fainted, check if trainer has more (yes: FORCE_SWITCH, no: BATTLE_END). FORCE_SWITCH: fainted Pokemon's trainer must choose replacement. BATTLE_END: display win/loss, distribute exp (optional), return to overworld or loot phase. This FSM orchestrates battle flow.

task.title: Create battle UI components
task.description: Create battle UI scenes: scenes/battle/battle_ui/battle_hud.tscn (two HP bar panels GBA style: Pokemon name/level/gender, HP bar with green>yellow>red gradient and smooth tween drain, status icon BRN/PSN/SLP/PAR/FRZ, optional EXP bar), scenes/battle/battle_ui/move_selector.tscn (2x2 grid of move buttons: name, PP remaining/max, type color background, type badge icon), scenes/battle/battle_ui/battle_menu.tscn (2x2 grid: FIGHT/BAG/POKEMON/RUN with GBA-styled rounded rectangles), scenes/battle/battle_ui/pokemon_switch_panel.tscn (vertical list of party Pokemon: icon/name/level/HP bar/status, fainted grayed out), scenes/battle/battle_ui/battle_bag.tscn (categorized item list: Potions/Pokeballs/Status Heals/Battle Items with tab buttons, tap to use), scenes/battle/battle_ui/battle_text_box.tscn (bottom text panel with typewriter effect, tap to advance/skip, auto-advance after delay). Implement corresponding .gd scripts for interaction logic. These UI components provide player control during battles.

task.title: Create battle visuals and animations
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_visuals/pokemon_battle_sprite.tscn: Sprite2D with AnimationPlayer for idle (subtle breathing scale oscillation), hit (flash white, shake, bounce back), faint (fall down, fade out), send out (Pokeball opens, sprite materializes), return (shrink into beam). Create scenes/battle/battle_visuals/move_animation_player.gd: per-type generic animations using GPUParticles2D (Normal: basic flash, Fire: flame particles, Water: splash, Grass: leaves, Electric: lightning bolt + screen flash, Ice: crystals, etc. for all 18 types). Screen shake via camera offset tween, screen flash via ColorRect alpha tween. Move animations play on defender's sprite position (attacking moves) or attacker (stat boosts). These animations bring battles to life visually.

task.title: Create full battle scene integrating engine and UI
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_scene.tscn: full battle UI scene with background (gradient or themed), both Pokemon sprites (front/back), HP bars, text box, menu system. Implement scenes/battle/battle_scene.gd: orchestrates battle by running battle_state_machine, consuming BattleEvent stream from battle_resolver, animating each event sequentially via move_animation_player and sprite animations, handling player input for action selection, calling battle_resolver for turn resolution. For local (wild/NPC) battles, runs entirely on local machine. For PvP, integrates with battle_net_controller. This ties together all battle systems into a playable experience.

task.title: Implement battle networking for PvP
task.description: Create scenes/battle/battle_net/battle_net_controller.gd: for PvP battles, server hosts BattleContext. Client sends action via @rpc('any_peer','reliable') _submit_battle_action(action_data). Server collects both actions, when both received resolves turn via battle_resolver, broadcasts results via @rpc('authority','reliable') _receive_battle_events(events). Both clients animate events locally. Server sends state checksum to verify sync (optional but recommended). Timer per action selection (60s, if timeout server picks random valid move or Struggle if no PP). Create scenes/battle/battle_net/battle_sync.gd: for spectators, server streams battle events to spectating peers (sees animations, no input). This enables multiplayer battles - the core of battle royale elimination.

task.title: Write comprehensive battle engine tests
task.description: Create extensive test suite: tests/unit/test_damage_calculator.gd (known damage ranges for specific matchups, verify STAB/type effectiveness/critical/weather/held item modifiers), tests/unit/test_stat_stages.gd (+6 Atk = 4x, -6 Def = 0.25x, verify clamp and reset on switch), tests/unit/test_status_effects.gd (Burn reduces HP, Paralysis prevents move 25% statistically over 1000 trials, Sleep lasts 1-3 turns, Freeze 20% thaw, type immunities), tests/unit/test_weather.gd (Sun boosts Fire weakens Water, Sandstorm/Hail damage non-immune, duration tracking), tests/unit/test_ability_effects.gd (test each implemented ability: Intimidate lowers Atk on switch, Levitate grants Ground immunity, etc.), tests/unit/test_held_items.gd (Life Orb recoil, Leftovers heal, Choice Band locks, Focus Sash OHKO survival), tests/unit/test_move_effects.gd (Swords Dance raises Atk by 2, Thunderbolt 10% Paralyze, Dragon Dance boosts Atk+Speed), tests/integration/test_battle_full_flow.gd (full battle simulation no UI: two trainers with known teams, verify turn order, fainting triggers switch, battle ends correctly), tests/network/test_battle_net_sync.gd (two instances PvP battle, both submit moves, both receive same events, state stays synced). All battle engine tests run headlessly without scenes since engine is pure data logic. This is the most heavily tested phase - battle accuracy is paramount.

task.title: Implement player inventory system
task.description: Extend resources/player_data.gd with bag: Dictionary[String, int] mapping item_id to quantity. Methods: add_item(item_id, quantity), remove_item(item_id, quantity), has_item(item_id) -> bool, get_item_count(item_id) -> int. Server-authoritative: all inventory changes go through server RPCs. This tracks items each player owns - consumed when used, granted when picked up.

task.title: Create item pickup system

On player interaction (A button while overlapping), send pickup request to server. Server validates item exists (not already picked up), grants item, removes pickup for all clients via MultiplayerSpawner despawn or RPC. Floating animation (gentle up/down bobbing tween), pickup particle effect (sparkle), pickup sound effect. Implement item spawn system in world.gd: on round start, server reads map def JSON for item spawn points, spawns item_pickup nodes via MultiplayerSpawner. Items can also spawn dynamically (loot drops from defeated players). Item pickups are a key exploration reward.

task.title: Create healing station system
task.description: Create scenes/world/interactables/healing_station.tscn: Area2D marking Pokemon Center heal zone. Implement scenes/world/interactables/healing_station.gd: when player interacts (A button), send heal request to server. Server heals all Pokemon in player's party (full HP, cure status, restore PP). Play healing jingle and animation (screen flash or Pokemon Center nurse dialogue). Usable unlimited times during roaming phase, no cooldown. Healing stations provide strategic points on maps where players can recover.

task.title: Create bag UI for item management
task.description: Create scenes/ui/menus/bag_view.tscn: category tabs (Pokeballs, Medicine, Battle Items, Held Items), scrollable item list per category showing icon/name/quantity, tap item to see description and USE/GIVE options. USE: context-dependent (Potions -> select Pokemon to heal, Status heals -> select Pokemon, Held items -> select Pokemon to hold). GIVE: assign held item to Pokemon. Accessible from pause menu during roaming and from battle menu during battles. Implement scenes/ui/menus/bag_view.gd for interaction logic. Bag UI provides item access - must be intuitive on mobile.

task.title: Integrate in-battle item usage
task.description: Integrate item usage into battle system (already scaffolded in battle_bag.tscn from battle UI task). Using item counts as player's action for the turn (like official games). Server validates item ownership, applies effect, deducts from inventory. Items usable in battle: Potions (heal HP), Status heals (cure status), Revives (revive fainted Pokemon), X Items (boost stat stages), Pokeballs (wild battles only, triggers catch mechanic). Implement server-side validation and effect application in battle_resolver. Items in battle add strategic options.

task.title: Write item system tests
task.description: Create tests/unit/test_item_system.gd: add items, remove items, verify counts; use Potion on damaged Pokemon verify HP restored; use Revive on fainted Pokemon verify revived; use X Attack verify stat stage increased. Create tests/network/test_item_pickup_sync.gd: player A picks up item, server removes it, player B cannot pick it up (race condition handling). Integration test: pick up item in overworld, verify appears in bag, use in battle, verify consumed. These tests validate item system correctness.

task.title: Create NPC trainer data and teams
task.description: Create data/npc_trainers/npc_teams.json: array of NPC definitions with {id, name, sprite, difficulty (1-5), team: [{species, level, moves, held_item}, ...]}. Multiple difficulty tiers for scaling across rounds. At least 20 NPC definitions covering all types and difficulties. NPCs fill tournament slots when needed and provide practice battles - variety matters.

task.title: Create NPC trainer overworld presence
task.description: Create scenes/world/npcs/npc_trainer.tscn: CharacterBody2D with sprite, collision, Area2D for line-of-sight detection. Implement scenes/world/npcs/npc_trainer.gd: NPCs stand in fixed positions or patrol short routes. Line-of-sight: RayCast2D or Area2D extending forward, if player enters LoS, NPC initiates battle (exclamation mark animation, walks toward player, battle starts). Server manages NPC state. NPC battles are single-player (server plays NPC side). NPCs add world liveliness and optional battles.

task.title: Implement NPC battle AI
task.description: Create scenes/world/npcs/npc_ai.gd to decide NPC battle actions. Difficulty 1 (Easy): random move selection. Difficulty 2 (Medium): prefer super-effective moves, switch if current Pokemon at type disadvantage and has better option. Difficulty 3 (Hard): factor stat stages/status/HP, use items, predict opponent switches. Difficulty 4-5 (Expert): optimal play considering speed tiers/priority/set-up sweeping. Algorithm: (1) score each move: base_power * STAB * type_effectiveness * (accuracy/100), (2) score switches: type advantage vs opponent + HP remaining, (3) score item usage: if HP low consider potion, if status consider heal, (4) pick highest-scoring action; at lower difficulties add randomness (multiply scores by randf_range(0.5, 1.5)). NPC AI provides challenge scaling - higher difficulties must feel competent.

task.title: Write NPC system tests
task.description: Create tests/unit/test_npc_ai.gd: given battle context with known Pokemon, verify AI picks super-effective move on Medium difficulty, verify AI switches when heavily disadvantaged on Hard, verify Easy produces varied selections. Integration test: walk into NPC LoS, battle triggers, NPC makes reasonable moves, battle concludes. These tests validate NPC AI works at different difficulty levels.

task.title: Implement round manager state machine
task.description: Create scenes/battle_royale/round_manager.gd as the core BR orchestrator. State machine: ROUND_START -> ROAMING -> MATCHMAKING -> BATTLING -> LOOT -> ROUND_END -> (next round or VICTORY). ROUND_START: server loads map for this round (from round_config.json or random from pool), spawns players at spawn points, spawns items, announces round number, sets wild Pokemon levels based on round. ROAMING: timer starts (5min configurable), players explore freely, timer visible to all, server tracks player states, warnings at 60s/30s/10s remaining, at 0 transition to MATCHMAKING. MATCHMAKING: server pairs surviving players for 1v1 battles (if odd number: bye or NPC), pairings announced, 5s countdown. BATTLING: all paired battles simultaneous, server runs each independently, players not in battle can roam or spectate. LOOT: after battles, losers eliminated, loot dropped at battle location, winners can pick up, 60s loot timer. ROUND_END: check win condition (1 player: VICTORY, else increment round, load next map, ROUND_START). VICTORY: display victory screen. This orchestrates the entire BR flow.

task.title: Implement matchmaker pairing logic
task.description: Create scenes/battle_royale/matchmaker.gd with pair_players(alive_players: Array[int]) -> Array[Array]. Shuffle players randomly, pair sequentially: [0,1], [2,3], [4,5], ... If odd player: pair with NPC or grant bye. Optional: seed-based pairing (rank by party total levels or round wins for strongest vs weakest). Returns array of pairs: [[peer_id_a, peer_id_b], [peer_id_c, peer_id_d], ...]. NPC opponents represented by negative IDs or special flag. Matchmaking determines battle pairings - fairness and unpredictability matter.

task.title: Implement elimination tracker
task.description: Create scenes/battle_royale/elimination_tracker.gd: maintains alive_players (Array[int] peer IDs) and eliminated_players (Array[int] in order). Methods: eliminate_player(peer_id) moves from alive to eliminated, emits EventBus.player_eliminated(peer_id); get_placement(peer_id) -> int returns finishing position (1st, 2nd, etc.); is_game_over() -> bool returns true when 1 player remains; get_winner() -> int returns last player standing. Track per-player stats: Pokemon caught, battles won, items used, Pokemon KO'd. This tracks game state and determines victory.

task.title: Implement loot drop system
task.description: Create scenes/battle_royale/loot_dropper.gd with drop_loot(loser_peer_id, battle_location). Server reads loser's party and bag, spawns item_pickup nodes at/near battle location for each item in bag, spawns pokemon_pickup nodes for each non-fainted Pokemon (or all, winner must heal fainted). Create scenes/battle_royale/pokemon_pickup.tscn: similar to item_pickup but contains serialized PokemonInstance, shows overworld icon and name/level on hover, on pickup: if party has room add to party, if full offer swap UI. Winner has priority pickup (first 30s only winner can pick up, then open to all). Loot drops reward winners and provide comeback mechanics.

task.title: Create round timer HUD
task.description: Create scenes/battle_royale/round_timer_hud.tscn: persistent on-screen timer in MM:SS format. Color changes: white (normal), yellow (<60s), red (<10s), pulsing red (<5s). Sound effect at 10-second mark (ticking). Server-authoritative: server ticks timer via @rpc or MultiplayerSynchronizer, clients display. Implement scenes/battle_royale/round_timer_hud.gd. Timer creates urgency and pacing - must be clearly visible.

task.title: Create player count display and spectator mode
task.description: Create scenes/battle_royale/player_count_display.tscn: 'X/Y Players Remaining' in corner of HUD, updates when player eliminated, brief animation on change (number ticks down). Create scenes/battle_royale/spectator_mode.tscn for eliminated players: free-roaming camera over map (not attached to player), cycle through watching remaining players with left/right buttons, if battle ongoing can watch (receives events via battle_sync.gd), cannot interact with world, optional chat for spectators. Implement corresponding .gd scripts. Spectator mode keeps eliminated players engaged.

task.title: Create victory screen
task.description: Create scenes/battle_royale/victory_screen.tscn: winner announcement with fanfare, winner's avatar and team displayed prominently, stats summary for all players (placement 1st/2nd/3rd, Pokemon caught, battles won/lost, total damage dealt, items used), Return to Lobby button. Implement scenes/battle_royale/victory_screen.gd to display stats from elimination_tracker. Victory screen provides closure and celebration.

task.title: Create map rotation system
task.description: Create data/maps/map_pool.json: defines which maps available and order (or random). Each round can have specific map or random from pool. Later rounds have maps with higher-level encounter tables and better items. Round manager loads maps dynamically from this config. Map rotation provides variety and progression.

task.title: Write Battle Royale flow tests
task.description: Create tests/integration/test_round_lifecycle.gd: simulate full round (start -> roam timer expires -> matchmaking produces valid pairs -> battles resolve -> loot drops -> next round starts), verify state transitions. Create tests/unit/test_matchmaker.gd: 8 players -> 4 pairs, 7 players -> 3 pairs + 1 NPC, 2 players -> 1 pair, 1 player -> victory. Create tests/integration/test_loot_drop.gd: eliminate player with 3 Pokemon and 5 items, verify 8 pickups spawned at correct location. Integration test: full 4-player game on LAN, play through 2 rounds, verify everything connects. These tests validate the core game loop.

task.title: Create glass-morphism UI theme
task.description: Create assets/shaders/glass_blur.gdshader: Gaussian blur shader for background behind UI panels, sample screen texture behind panel, apply blur + color tint + border glow. Create scenes/ui/components/glass_panel.tscn: reusable PanelContainer with glass shader via ShaderMaterial on ColorRect background, semi-transparent white/blue tint, rounded corners via StyleBoxFlat. Create resources/themes/main_theme.tres: global Godot theme defining font (pixel for GBA feel or modern sans-serif for premium, hybrid: pixel for battle text, clean for menus), button styles (rounded, glass-like, with press animation), color palette (Pokemon-inspired: reds, whites, dark blues). Apply glass panel to: lobby player list, battle menu, bag view, pause menu, party view, move selector, all dialog boxes. Glass-morphism creates a premium aesthetic.

task.title: Create screen transition system
task.description: Create scenes/ui/components/screen_transition.tscn: CanvasLayer (always on top) with ColorRect + shader. Transition types: horizontal wipe, diagonal wipe, fade to black, iris wipe (circle), GBA-style battle encounter stripes. Create assets/shaders/transition_wipe.gdshader: uses gradient texture as mask, animate threshold uniform 0 to 1 to reveal/hide. API: ScreenTransition.play('wipe_left', 0.5) returns signal when complete. All scene changes use this: title->lobby, lobby->world, world->battle, round transitions. Transitions add polish and visual continuity.

task.title: Enhance battle animations with particles and effects
task.description: Enhance battle visuals (from earlier battle animations task): per-type particle systems with proper colors and motion (Fire: orange/red particles rising + warm screen tint, Water: blue splash + waves, Electric: yellow sparks + screen flash, Grass: green leaf particles, Ice: white/blue crystals + cool tint, etc. for all 18 types). Hit effects: screen shake intensity scales with damage, super-effective has bigger shake + larger flash, not-very-effective minimal shake. Critical hit: brief time-slow effect (0.8x speed for 0.3s) + extra flash. Faint animation: sprite falls, grayscale shader, sad sound. Level up: golden particles rising, stat display. These enhancements make battles feel impactful.

task.title: Create HP bar with smooth drain animation
task.description: Enhance scenes/battle/battle_ui/battle_hud.tscn HP bars (or create scenes/ui/components/hp_bar.tscn): custom TextureProgressBar or Control with draw override. Color gradient: green (100-50%), yellow (50-20%), red (20-0%). Drain animation: smooth tween over ~1s, if large damage speed up slightly. 'Trailing' effect: actual HP drops immediately, second bar trails behind slowly (like fighting games). HP bars provide critical battle feedback - smooth animation feels professional.

task.title: Polish Pokemon catch animation
task.description: Enhance scenes/encounter/pokeball_animation.tscn (from earlier catch task): Pokeball arcs with motion blur, Pokemon dissolves into sparkles when entering ball, each shake: ball tilts 30°, pauses, tilts -30°, pauses; break-free: ball opens with burst particle, Pokemon reforms from sparkles; catch success: starburst particle effect, ball glows, congratulatory text with Pokemon name. Catching is a highlight moment - animation must feel rewarding.

task.title: Add overworld polish effects
task.description: Add polish to world scene: tall grass sway animation when walked through, water tiles with animated reflections (shader or animated tileset), optional day/night cycle (use CanvasModulate with color tween - optional for BR since rounds are short but adds ambiance), footstep particles on different terrain (dust on dirt, splashes on water edge), item pickup: item floats up to HUD 'bag' icon with particle trail. These details create immersion.

task.title: Implement haptic feedback for iOS
task.description: Use Godot's Input.vibrate_handheld() or GDExtension/plugin for iOS haptic engine. Trigger haptics on: button press (light), move hit (medium), critical hit (heavy), Pokemon caught (medium), item pickup (light), super-effective hit (heavy). Integrate haptic calls throughout UI and battle systems. Haptic feedback enhances mobile feel - iOS users expect it.

task.title: Create toast notification system
task.description: Create scenes/ui/components/toast_notification.tscn: slide-in notification from top of screen, used for: 'Player X was eliminated!', 'Round 2 starting!', 'New item found!', 'Timer: 60 seconds remaining!'. Auto-dismiss after 3s, queue if multiple, semi-transparent glass style. Implement toast manager to handle queueing and display. Toasts provide non-intrusive event notifications.

task.title: Implement AudioManager with music crossfade
task.description: Implement autoloads/audio_manager.gd with two AudioStreamPlayer nodes for music (music_a, music_b). Crossfade: play_music(track, fade_duration=1.0): if music_a playing, start music_b with new track at volume 0, tween music_a to 0 and music_b to target volume over fade_duration, swap roles. Music tracks loaded from assets/audio/music/ by name. Music plays at reduced volume during battles (or switches to battle music). SFX pool: 8 AudioStreamPlayer nodes for concurrent effects, play_sfx(sfx): find idle player, load and play. Cry player: dedicated AudioStreamPlayer, play_cry(dex_number): load assets/audio/cries/{dex_number}.ogg. Cries play on encounter, send-out, Pokedex view. Audio manager provides centralized audio control.

task.title: Configure audio bus layout
task.description: Create default_bus_layout.tres: Master bus, Music bus (child of Master, volume controllable in settings), SFX bus (child of Master, volume controllable), Cries bus (child of SFX, slightly lower volume). Assign each AudioStreamPlayer in AudioManager to respective bus. Bus layout enables volume control per category.

task.title: Source and integrate music tracks
task.description: Source music tracks (GBA game rips as placeholders, plan for original compositions or royalty-free for distribution): title screen theme, lobby theme (upbeat), town/safe zone theme (calm GBA-style), route/wilderness theme (adventurous), cave theme (mysterious), forest theme (natural), wild battle theme (energetic), trainer battle theme (intense), final battle theme (epic), victory fanfare (short), defeat jingle (short), round transition music, game over/elimination jingle. Place in assets/audio/music/. Document sources in assets/audio/README.md for legal compliance.

task.title: Implement context-sensitive music system
task.description: Integrate AudioManager calls throughout: world.gd tells AudioManager which track based on map's zone type, battle_scene.gd switches to battle music on start and reverts on end, round_manager.gd plays round transition music between rounds. Music fades out during screen transitions, fades in after. Low HP warning: when player's active Pokemon <20% HP in battle, overlay rapid beeping SFX or switch to tense battle music variant. Context-sensitive music enhances immersion.

task.title: Source and integrate SFX
task.description: Source sound effects (from Sounds Resource FRLG or similar, document for legal compliance): menu (button press, hover, tab switch, back, error buzz), overworld (footsteps per-terrain, tall grass rustle, item pickup sparkle, heal jingle, NPC exclamation), battle (move hit generic + type-specific, critical hit emphasis, stat change chime, status apply/cure, weather start, Pokemon faint, switch, Pokeball throw/shake/catch/break-free), BR (timer warning beeps, elimination announcement, round start horn, victory fanfare). Place in assets/audio/sfx/. Integrate SFX calls at all interaction points throughout UI, world, and battle systems. SFX provide essential feedback.

task.title: Optimize for iOS performance
task.description: Profile on target iOS devices (iPhone 12+ minimum). Optimizations: ensure only visible TileMapLayer tiles processed, use rendering/2d/options/use_gpu_pixel_snap for crisp pixels, particle budget: limit max particles per system, use GPUParticles2D over CPUParticles2D, object pooling for frequently spawned/despawned nodes (battle effects, item pickups), memory: preload common resources, lazy-load rare ones (Pokemon sprites loaded on encounter not all at startup), texture compression: use ETC2 for iOS (import settings in .godot/imported/), audio compression: OGG Vorbis for music, WAV for short SFX (lower latency). Target: 60fps constant, <200MB memory, <500MB install size. Performance optimization ensures smooth mobile experience.

task.title: Refine touch input for iOS
task.description: Refine virtual joystick: test dead zone values on physical device, adjust for finger size, test haptic feedback integration, ensure joystick doesn't interfere with other touch targets, consider 'floating' joystick (appears where you first touch on left side) vs fixed position (floating preferred for mobile). Button sizes: minimum 44x44 points (Apple HIG) for all interactive elements. Battle UI: ensure move buttons and menu items large enough for comfortable tapping. Optional: pinch-to-zoom on minimap. Prevent accidental taps: add brief delay or require deliberate press for destructive actions (using items, fleeing). Touch refinement makes mobile controls feel native.

task.title: Finalize iOS export configuration
task.description: Complete export_presets.cfg: bundle identifier (com.yourname.pokemonbr), minimum iOS 15.0, required capabilities (none beyond default), entitlements (com.apple.developer.networking.multicast for UDP), device orientation (Landscape), launch screen storyboard, app icons (all required sizes). Provisioning: Development profile for testing, Ad Hoc or TestFlight for distribution. Xcode project modifications: Info.plist add NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription ('This app uses local network to discover and connect to nearby players.'), add NSBonjourServices if needed (raw UDP so likely not needed). This completes iOS platform configuration.

task.title: Test and handle iOS networking quirks
task.description: Test UDP broadcast on iOS: test on same WiFi with multiple iOS devices, test iOS and macOS mixed. iOS may restrict broadcast on cellular (shouldn't matter for LAN/WiFi), may show 'Local Network' permission prompt on first use - handle denial case (show error message, fall back to manual IP entry). ENet over WiFi: test with varying signal strengths, verify reconnect behavior. Document any iOS-specific networking limitations.

task.title: Implement battery and thermal optimizations
task.description: Battery/thermal optimizations: reduce frame rate to 30fps during lobby/menus (less GPU work), Engine.max_fps = 30 in lobby, Engine.max_fps = 60 in game. Audio: use hardware-decoded formats where possible. Networking: don't poll more frequently than needed (UDP broadcast every 2s is fine). These optimizations extend battery life and prevent thermal throttling.

task.title: Implement safe area handling for iPhone
task.description: Account for iPhone notch/Dynamic Island and home indicator. Use DisplayServer.get_display_safe_area() to position HUD elements within safe margins. All critical UI (timer, buttons, minimap) must be within safe area. Test on devices with different notch/island configurations. Safe area handling prevents UI being obscured by notch.

task.title: Create comprehensive edge case test suite
task.description: Add edge case tests: battle with Pokemon knowing only status moves running out of PP (Struggle mechanic), battle where both Pokemon faint same turn (speed tie resolution), player disconnects mid-battle (forfeit, opponent wins), player disconnects during roaming (remove from alive players, drop loot), host migration (if host disconnects game ends - document limitation or implement host migration as stretch), all players ready then one unreadies quickly, item used on full HP Pokemon (no effect, don't consume), Revive used on non-fainted Pokemon (should fail), party full when catching Pokemon (swap or release prompt), player tries to pick up item another player just grabbed (race condition). These tests catch corner cases.

task.title: Create network stress testing suite
task.description: Enhance ci/scripts/multi_instance_test.sh to launch 8 Godot instances on macOS: instance 0 auto-hosts, instances 1-7 auto-join at 127.0.0.1, all run automated gameplay (random movement, auto-catch, auto-battle with random moves). Run for 30 minutes, check for crashes/desyncs/memory leaks. Network condition simulation: use macOS pfctl or dnctl to add latency (50ms, 100ms, 200ms) and packet loss (1%, 5%, 10%), verify game remains playable at 100ms latency + 1% loss, verify graceful degradation at 200ms/5%. 8-player simultaneous battle phase: 4 battles running at once, verify server handles all without lag. Stress testing validates network robustness.

task.title: Tune game balance values
task.description: Create data/config/game_balance.json with all balance values: roaming timer per round (recommend: Round 1: 5min, Round 2: 4min, Round 3: 3min, Finals: 2min), wild encounter chance per step (15-20%), wild Pokemon level ranges per round (Round 1: 5-15, Round 2: 15-25, Round 3: 25-35, Finals: 35-50), item spawn quantities and quality per round, starter Pokemon level (5), catch rate modifier (1.0 = vanilla, can increase for faster games), NPC difficulty scaling per round, action timer in PvP battles (60s recommended), loot phase duration (60s). All values in JSON so easily tunable. Playtest with real players, iterate on values. Balance tuning makes the game fun - requires playtesting.

task.title: Implement error handling and recovery
task.description: Wrap all RPC calls with validation. Server validates all client requests: can't use items you don't have, can't pick up items that don't exist, can't submit battle actions out of turn. Client shows error toasts for rejected actions. Graceful handling: server crash (clients return to title with 'Host disconnected'), client crash (server removes player, continues game), network timeout (configurable 10s, auto-disconnect), invalid data (log warnings, don't crash). Error handling creates robustness.

task.title: Audit for memory leaks
task.description: Monitor memory usage over extended play sessions. Ensure all scenes properly freed on transition. Ensure all signal connections disconnected when nodes freed (use connect(signal, callable, CONNECT_ONE_SHOT) where appropriate, ensure queue_free() handles cleanup). Check for orphaned nodes (nodes removed from tree but not freed). Use Godot's memory profiler to identify leaks. Memory leak prevention ensures long-term stability.

task.title: Conduct final integration testing
task.description: Final integration testing: minimum 5 full playthroughs with 4+ players before considering complete. Test scenarios: full 8-player game, 2-player game (minimal), odd number of players (7, 5, 3), player disconnect during various phases, NPC battles, all item types, all status effects, all weather conditions, catching Pokemon with full party, using all UI screens. Document any issues found. CI pipeline runs full test suite on every commit. This validates the complete game experience.

## NetworkManager autoload scope

- When a task spec mixes autoload plumbing with UI navigation ("on disconnect, return to title screen with error message"), implement only the autoload-layer state changes (`players.clear()`, `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = null`) and leave scene transitions to a scene-level handler. Reason: the autoload has no authoritative view of which scene is active or which error UI to surface, and the title scene may not yet exist when the RPC layer is being built. How to apply: when reviewing a NetworkManager-related spec, split UI-transition asks out as a follow-up rather than coupling the singleton to a specific scene flow.

## Headless Godot resource creation

- Run `godot --headless --import <path>` before any script that creates `.tres` resources referencing imported assets: `--import` runs the full asset pipeline, writing `.import` sidecars and `.ctex` files into `.godot/imported/`. Without it, `load("res://*.png")` either fails or falls back to embedding raw pixels, and class names won't register so GUT refuses to run. (Not `--editor --quit`.)
- Use `SceneTree` + `_init()` + `quit()` for headless resource authoring: a script extending `SceneTree` with all logic in `_init()` is the minimal viable harness — no `_process` loop, no editor mode. `ResourceSaver.save()` writes the `.tres` and `quit()` exits cleanly.
- Always `load("res://path.png")` to get a texture reference; never `Image.create()` + `ImageTexture.create_from_image()`: the latter serializes raw pixel data into the `.tres` (a 256×256 image becomes ~900KB inline), while `load()` after `--import` produces a tiny `ExtResource` reference — the diff for both tilesets shipped at <30 lines each.

tasks.title: Initialize Godot project with basic configuration
tasks.description: Create a Godot 4.4.x project (4.5 not yet released - see docs/GODOT_VERSION_STATUS.md) with proper display settings, directory structure, and git setup. Configure project.godot for iPhone display (1170x2532), landscape orientation, stretch mode canvas_items, aspect keep_height. Create all directory folders per CODEBASE.md structure. Set up .gitignore for Godot projects (ignore .godot/, keep *.import). Initialize git repository. This is the foundation for all subsequent work - every other task depends on having a working Godot project structure.

tasks.title: Install and configure GUT test framework
tasks.description: Install GUT addon to addons/gut/ directory and configure for headless CLI execution. Create gut_config.json to enable command-line test running. Verify tests can run headlessly via `godot --headless`. Create a sanity test (test_sanity.gd) that asserts true to validate the setup. GUT will be used throughout development for unit and integration testing, so this must work before any test-driven development begins. CRITICAL: Godot binary is /Applications/Godot_mono.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot on macOS (no godot on PATH). Headless GUT MUST use the -s flag: Godot --headless --path "$PWD" -s addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd -gconfig=res://gut_config.json -gexit. Omitting -s pops a blocking GUI modal.

tasks.title: Install and configure GdUnit4 test framework
tasks.description: Install GdUnit4 addon to addons/gdunit4/ directory. Verify it runs headlessly alongside GUT. Both test frameworks will be used: GUT for integration tests and GdUnit4 for unit tests. Create a simple GdUnit4 test to validate setup. Ensure both frameworks coexist without conflicts. CRITICAL: Godot binary is /Applications/Godot_mono.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot on macOS (no godot on PATH). Any headless Godot invocation MUST pass --path "$PWD" and -s <script.gd>. Omitting -s pops a blocking macOS GUI modal and freezes the session.

tasks.title: Create autoload singleton scaffolds
tasks.description: Create the 5 core autoload singletons as empty GDScript files and register them in project.godot under [autoload]: GameManager (top-level FSM), NetworkManager (ENet networking), EventBus (signal hub), AudioManager (music/SFX), DataRegistry (game data loader). Each should be a minimal class extending Node with a _ready() function that prints its name. These singletons form the architectural backbone - all game systems will interact through these autoloads.

Create a basic title_screen.tscn with a centered Label showing 'Pokemon LAN Battle Royale' and placeholder buttons for Host/Join. The main scene should be set as the project's main scene in project.godot. This establishes the scene management pattern and entry point for the application.

Configure app icons and launch screen. Add NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription to Info.plist template. This enables building for iOS - critical for the target platform.

tasks.title: Create Pokemon registry JSON for Gen 1
tasks.description: Create data/pokemon/pokemon_registry.json with all 151 Gen 1 Pokemon. Each entry needs: dex_number, name, types, base_stats (hp/atk/def/spa/spd/spe), abilities (Gen 3+ ability list), learnset (level-up moves for Gen 3), catch_rate, base_exp, growth_rate, egg_groups, sprite paths. Source data from PokeAPI or Veekun pokedex database. This is a large data entry task but foundational - all Pokemon content depends on this registry being complete and accurate.

tasks.title: Create move registry JSON
tasks.description: Create data/moves/move_registry.json with ~200 moves covering all types and categories. Each entry: id, name, type, category (Physical/Special/Status), power, accuracy, pp, priority, target, effect description, effect_chance, stat_changes dict, status_inflict, flags array. Include all moves referenced in Gen 1 Pokemon learnsets. Reference Pokemon Showdown or Bulbapedia for accurate move data. Moves are used constantly in battle - accuracy matters. IMPORTANT: incremental write strategy required. The dataset is too large to materialize in one pass — DO NOT think the entire registry through before writing. Instead: (1) Write data/moves/move_registry.json with the JSON skeleton + first 20 moves immediately. (2) Then Edit-append remaining moves in batches of 20-30 at a time, committing the file with each batch. Never accumulate 200+ items in extended thinking before writing — that exhausts the output token budget.

tasks.title: Create item and ability registries
tasks.description: Create data/items/item_registry.json (~50 items: Pokeballs, Potions, Status heals, Revives, Battle items, Held items) and data/abilities/ability_registry.json (~50 common abilities: Overgrow, Blaze, Torrent, Intimidate, Levitate, Static, Poison Point, Thick Fat, Sturdy, etc.). These registries enable the item system and ability-triggered battle mechanics. IMPORTANT: incremental write strategy required. Two separate registry files (~50 each). For each file: (1) Write the JSON skeleton + first 15-20 entries immediately. (2) Then Edit-append remaining entries in batches of 15-20, committing the file with each batch. Never accumulate all entries in extended thinking before writing — that exhausts the output token budget. Write items first, then abilities.
